# Calendar parity fixtures

Synthetic inputs only. `cases.json` includes the 34 feasibility examples plus
the remaining branches of all 30 existing Rust calendar tests and additional
validation boundaries. `coverage.json` maps every Rust test to its input cases.
Large inputs use a repeat descriptor materialized by the runners.

`expected.json` was frozen from the Rust engine at the verified baseline; it is
not regenerated by tests. Its calendar dates, event counts, occurrence keys,
errors and transitions were checked against `daemon/tests/calendar.rs`.
The comparison canonicalizes timed instants to UTC, preserving date-only
values, field identity, context, ordering, titles and exact error codes.

Run `./scripts/test-calendar-parity.py --engine both`. Rust is a test oracle
only. The GJS run also checks that both a slow single iterator call and an
impossible recurrence stop at an internal deadline in a disposable process.

The US/Eastern alias is an explicit engine-specific expectation: this libical
build rejects it, while the public edition supports it through the required
full IANA alias data. Its UTC instant is specified literally. Other cases
compare the same frozen result for both engines. Extra cases cover malformed
current dates, impossible yearly rules, several regions and aliases, and
custom timezone isolation between calls.
